findings.who: A disabled worker whose SSDI benefit was reduced to zero all year because of the workers' compensation offset. SSA still issues a Form SSA-1099 showing the offset amount in box 3 as benefits paid.
findings.why_no: No check arrived, so truthfully they did not 'get social security benefits.' The help names only Medicare premiums and debt as withheld amounts that count, which reads as the complete list of exceptions.
findings.irs_text: p915 p. 5: "Your gross benefits are shown in box 3 of Form SSA-1099 or RRB-1099... The amount in box 5 shows your net benefits for 2025 (box 3 minus box 4). Use the amount in box 5 to figure whether any of your benefits are taxable." (Pub. 915 also treats a workers' compensation offset as a social security benefit.)
findings.fix: Ask about the form, not cash received: 'Did you or your spouse receive a Form SSA-1099 or RRB-1099 for 2025, even one showing that benefits were withheld, offset or repaid?' Add to the help: 'Answer Yes even if you received no payment, for example because workers' compensation, Medicare premiums, tax withholding or a debt offset took the whole benefit.'

findings.who: A filer, or a spouse on a joint return, who receives Social Security Disability Insurance, survivor benefits or spousal benefits. They think of 'social security' as their own retirement benefit.
findings.why_no: The question says 'social security benefits' without naming disability or survivor benefits. The filer reads their monthly 'disability' payment as something different.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 31: "Disability payments... (including Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) payments)"... "You must report the remaining $12,000 on line 6a."
findings.fix: Reword to 'social security benefits of any kind (retirement, disability (SSDI), survivor, spouse's)' and add to the help that SSI is not included.

findings.who: A retired railroad worker, or the spouse of one, who receives a monthly annuity from the Railroad Retirement Board and gets both Form RRB-1099 and Form RRB-1099-R.
findings.why_no: The filer cannot tell whether their annuity is 'railroad retirement benefits treated as social security.' They see it as a railroad pension, report it as a pension, and answer no.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 31: "If you received railroad retirement benefits treated as social security, you should receive a Form RRB-1099."
findings.fix: Ask about something the filer can check: 'Did you or your spouse receive a Form RRB-1099 (not only an RRB-1099-R) from the Railroad Retirement Board?' Then classify the benefit after a yes.

findings.who: A U.S. resident who receives Canada Pension Plan, Quebec Pension Plan or Old Age Security payments, or a German statutory pension (gesetzliche Rente), and gets no Form SSA-1099 or RRB-1099.
findings.why_no: The question itself says 'Form SSA-1099 or Form RRB-1099 reports them,' and they have neither form. The help also says 'a state pension from any other country is not this,' and they read their CPP or German Rente as exactly that, so they list it as other income.
findings.irs_text: p915 p. 6: "social security benefits paid by those countries to U.S. residents are treated for U.S. income tax purposes as if they were paid under the social security legislation of the United States. If you receive social security benefits from Canada or Germany, include them on line 1 of Worksheet 1."
findings.fix: Ask a separate gate question: 'Did you or your spouse receive Canada Pension Plan, Quebec Pension Plan, Old Age Security, or German statutory pension (Deutsche Rentenversicherung) payments?' Remove the form reference from the main question, or add 'or a Canadian or German benefit statement.' Exclude only state pensions from other countries.

findings.who: A child or young adult filing their own return whose survivor or dependent benefits were paid to a parent or other representative payee.
findings.why_no: The money went to the parent, so the filer did not 'get' it. The help speaks only from the parent's side ('benefits that belong to your child are not yours') and never says that benefits paid to a payee for you are yours.
findings.irs_text: p915 p. 5: "Benefits are included in the taxable income (to the extent they are taxable) of the person who has the legal right to receive the benefits."
findings.fix: Add to the help: 'Answer Yes if benefits were paid in your name or for you, even if a parent or other representative payee received them.'

findings.who: A green card holder living abroad whose benefits were reported on Form SSA-1042S instead of Form SSA-1099, with 30% tax withheld in error.
findings.why_no: The question and the gated line both point to Form SSA-1099 and box 5. The filer holds a different form and may decide the question does not apply.
findings.irs_text: p915 p. 5: "If you are a green card holder and tax was withheld in error on your social security benefits because you have a foreign address... attach... A copy of the Form SSA-1042S."
findings.fix: Name Form SSA-1042S and Form RRB-1042S in the help, and say how to find the net benefit amount on those forms.

findings.who: A retired railroad worker, or that worker's spouse on a joint return, receives tier 1 railroad retirement benefits on Form RRB-1099 and no Form SSA-1099. The 2025 payments include a retroactive amount for 2023 or 2024.
findings.why_no: The question says 'The Form SSA-1099 says so in its description of the amount in box 3.' The filer has no SSA-1099, may not think of tier 1 railroad benefits as social security, and answers no. The RRB-1099 shows prior-year amounts in its own boxes, which the question never mentions.
findings.line: ssb.lump_sum (missed refusal; the lump-sum election that could lower taxable benefits is silently forgone)
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 31, Lines 6a and 6b: 'If you received railroad retirement benefits treated as social security, you should receive a Form RRB-1099.' Line 6c: 'If any of your benefits are taxable for 2025 and they include a lump-sum benefit payment that was for an earlier year, you may be able to reduce the taxable amount with the lump-sum election.'
findings.fix: Did the 2025 social security or tier 1 railroad retirement benefits paid to you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) include a payment for an earlier year? Form SSA-1099 shows this in the description of the box 3 amount. Form RRB-1099 shows it as amounts paid in 2025 for earlier years.

findings.who: An SSDI claimant was approved in 2025 with back pay to 2023. SSA paid part of the back pay directly to the claimant's attorney as fees and withheld part to offset SSI already received. The claimant got only a small check or none.
findings.why_no: The question asks whether benefits 'paid to you' included a payment for an earlier year. The filer reads 'paid to you' as money they actually received and answers no, even though the withheld and redirected amounts count as benefits paid to them.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 31, Line 6c: 'they include a lump-sum benefit payment that was for an earlier year, you may be able to reduce the taxable amount with the lump-sum election.' Also p. 31: 'Form SSA-1099 showing in box 3 the total social security benefits paid to you.'
findings.fix: Add to the help: 'Count back pay for earlier years even if part of it went to an attorney or was withheld to repay SSI or an overpayment.'

findings.who: A disability award was decided and paid in 2025. It covers months in 2024 and 2025 and is paid as one retroactive lump sum.
findings.why_no: The filer thinks of the award as a 2025 payment because it was decided and paid in 2025. They do not read the help's pointer to the box 3 description and answer that nothing was 'for an earlier year.'
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 32, Social Security Benefits Worksheet TIP: 'If any of your benefits are taxable for 2025 and they include a lump-sum benefit payment that was for an earlier year, you may be able to reduce the taxable amount.'
findings.fix: Name the common case in the question: 'This includes back pay from a disability or retirement award that covers months before 2025.'

locators: p. 31, Line 6c; p. 32, Social Security Benefits Worksheet, TIP
